before.summary: ChemCollapse wins — Tricastles of Lucenia locks Razorgale, then Seiryuu's Command

beats.text: ChemCollapse uses Beseech the Winds to reach Guo Jia level one on turn one and builds quest counters with Scout the Land and Tangu. Jett responds with Fluffy Shopkeep, Backup Charger, and Windmill Engineer's Reclaim and trades.

After Dungeon Guide takes Guo Jia to level three, ChemCollapse plays Tricastles of Lucenia, preventing non-advanced element card activations. Once per turn, any player may banish a norm or advanced element card from hand to make Tricastles lose all abilities until end of turn.

ChemCollapse follows with Uther (removing a Razorgale), Aella and a Royal Oathguard. Jett plays three Dream Fairies, a Zephyr and Purifying Thurible but drops below six cards, which turns off Ensnaring Fumes. Aella suppresses Jett's Essence Crucible.
ChemCollapse flips Seiryuu, plays Seiryuu's Command (triple on-enter) to generate an Arcane Blast and empower it by eight. The Blast costs nothing and finishes Jett.

before.summary: Jett wins — Aesan Protector chip damage, then Zephyr and Veiling Breeze on the last Razorgale trigger

beats.text: Jett brings in Turbo Charge, plays Windmill Engineer and Aesan Protector early, and wants a board that can kill Tricastles of Lucenia in two turns. Fairy Whispers finds Razorgale Calling.
ChemCollapse levels with Beseech and Dungeon Guide and draws with Incandescent Reliquary, but a Tricastle banished by Throne-keeper mill and a Purifying Thurible deny him the lock.

Jett plays two Razorgales and Essence Crucible with Distilled Water potions. Imperial Countermeasure absorbs the first trigger. Jett Zephyrs his own Aesan Protector and then uses Veiling Breeze as the final Razorgale trigger for lethal. The Aesan Protector is the MVP of the game.

beats.text: DuckHats has an amazing hand with an ultimate spell and a Ghosts of Pendragon, but he cannot find the Dungeon Guide to get to level three. ProAnnn goes up to Alice level two with Phantasmagoria and ships the rest of the graveyard to the bottom of the deck to mill two instead.

ProAnnn finds an Engulf and a Dynastic Whirlpool; the casters count the deck at about 27 cards, so two whirlpools are enough. A Bauble of Abundance gives ProAnnn extra draws, and without the Enfeebling Orb in play DuckHats cannot deny any activations.

The casters call the mill of 15 a done deal. They note that ProAnnn forgot his Lost Providence in game one but now remembers it. Two Dynastic Whirlpools finish DuckHats's deck, and ProAnnn ties the match.

before.summary: DuckHats wins — main-deck Cleansing Reunion and Reflected Blight stop the Whirlpool plan, and ProAnnn scoops with no recovery

beats.text: DuckHats holds the third Dungeon Guide and does not activate it in the recollection phase, the way many players would. He pays Escape the Wreckage with the Dungeon Guide in memory as a bait, and the casters say ProAnnn has to decide whether to take it.

DuckHats tries again to take down the Angel Attendant for a draw. He has a Reflected Blight in the graveyard, and the casters say it stops a spell from resolving and does not go under Alice as a curse. The Cleansing Reunion and Reflected Blight, in the main deck, are the choices DuckHats made for this event.

ProAnnn tries a Dynastic Whirlpool plus a second one back in the deck, but DuckHats's Cleansing Reunion answers it. ProAnnn has only a Resolute Stand and no recovery, so he scoops the game. DuckHats wins the match 2-1 and goes 1-0, and the casters note his main-deck reads of the room.

TeamTrueCaban pays Acquiescing Rejection, but two cards are not enough to save him. Baleful Oblation resolves, the units go to the graveyard, and the Measure of Arar delivers the final blow.
